Let’s dive into Chapter 6: Deepening the Practice—Advanced Auditing Techniques and Self-Application.
Now that you’ve got the basics of auditing down, it’s time to take things to the next level. As you start feeling more comfortable with simple recall and guided exploration, you might notice there are deeper layers to uncover. Advanced techniques are here to help you work through those more complex, or even hidden, experiences—gently peeling back the layers, like an onion, to get closer to your core self.
One of the most powerful tools at this stage is working with what’s called “chains.” Imagine you keep bumping into the same feeling—maybe rejection—over and over again, across different memories and moments in your life. These aren’t just random; they’re connected, forming a chain of related incidents that share a common theme or emotional tone.
Here’s how you can start working with chains:
First, notice any recurring themes or emotions that pop up during your auditing sessions. Next, try to follow that chain of memories backward, tracing each link all the way to the earliest incident, even if it seems minor or almost forgotten. As you address each link in the chain, you’ll start to notice insights and emotional releases building up, one after the other.
Another advanced strategy to consider is self-auditing. This is where you become your own guide, moving through the process without an external auditor. Of course, this takes a bit more self-awareness and honesty. It means keeping up a supportive inner conversation and being patient with yourself along the way. Self-auditing is great for ongoing growth, tackling new challenges as they show up, or simply if you’d rather work on your own.
Here are a few ways to make self-auditing work for you:
Set aside regular, quiet time just for self-reflection and recall. You might find it helpful to use written prompts or keep a journal to give some structure to your thoughts and track your progress. And above all, practice self-compassion and patience. Some memories might take a while to surface or resolve, and that’s perfectly okay.
Remember, these advanced techniques aren’t meant to replace the basics—they’re here to build on them. As you gain confidence and skill, you can really make this process your own. The door opens to new areas of growth, healing, and self-discovery—one layer at a time.
